messages:
Maya: Quick follow-up from the modularization RFC — proposal for a 6-month 'service cleanup' initiative. Goal: reduce cross-service coupling on the hot path (request-router -> enricher -> cache) and amortize tech debt into discrete slices. Thoughts?
Sam: Sounds good. do we have concrete success criteria? e.g. remove N shared interfaces, reduce p95 latency by X ms, and cut operational incidents by Y/month?
Maya: Yep — thinking metrics: p50/p95 latency on end-to-end inference, number of runtime coupling edges (owned by >1 service), and deploy blast radius size. Also want cost delta per 1M requests.
Tariq: +1 on measurable goals. Suggest we prioritize by "cost of change" vs customer impact. Some edges are cheap to peel, others will need schema migrations.
Elaine: Data migration question: if we extract the enrichment store, do we do a dual-write or a backfill? Dual-write adds complexity to writes; backfill can be slow. we need a plan per-slice.
Maya: Agreed. my thinking: triage each slice into one of three paths: (1) adapter facade (low-risk), (2) dual-write + backfill (medium), (3) live cutover with transactional migration (high-risk). We'll document per-slice plan.
Sam: For the cache/KV ownership — if we move KV ownership out of request-router, we must preserve hot-key locality. Any change that increases cross-pod lookups will blow up latency. Need a safety gate on p95.
Tariq: We can prototype a shard-aware sidecar in a 2-week spike to validate locality without full rollout. keep it behind a feature flag and a traffic mirror.
Maya: Good plan. propose spike owners: @Tariq for sidecar prototype, @Sam for metrics/failure-mode harness, @Elaine for migration playbook. Spike deliverables: design doc, perf numbers, failure-mode checklist.
Elaine: I'll draft migration playbook template. includes: downtime window (if any), backfill command sample, rollback steps, and data-consistency checks.
Sam: Can we add automated tests for compatibility? contract tests + a chaos test that kills the old path and verifies responses.
Tariq: Yep. I'll wire up a small harness that runs golden prompt sets against both paths and compares responses + latency.
infra-bot: CI: nightly/perf-run triggered for branch "modular-spike/tariq" — logs at https://ci.redwood.internal/1234 :construction:
Maya: timeline idea: month 0-1 spikes, month 2-4 iterative extraction for 3 low-risk slices, month 5-6 medium-risk cutovers, then reassess. open to feedback.
Sam: One more ask: let's define an "ownership transfer" checklist so code review can't merge extraction work without ops sign-off. items: telemetry, runbooks, quotas, infra cost estimate.
Maya: added. I'll create a short GH template and Confluence checklist tonight.
Elaine: :thumbsup: I'll sync with support on rollback comms.
Tariq: I'm starting the sidecar spike tomorrow. will post updates in this thread.
Maya: Awesome. next steps: owners start spikes, we convene weekly sync (30m) for the initiative. Thanks everyone.
